GAME TIME

Basketball School

## GAME TIME

is where players participate in different activities and games designed to stimulate their growth and development.

These activities have been carefully created to mimic the game of basketball. With the NBA Basketball School Camp Curriculum, players develop technically and tactically through the actual act of playing basketball itself.

Each Game Time activity is clearly described and presented in the following format: name, time, space, equipment, description, scoring, types of loads, staff roles, key concepts, and guiding questions. Coaches are encouraged to utilize the information presented and to expand on those ideas in a way that would be most meaningful to their players.

GAME TIME

Basketball School

2-ON-1+1 CLOSEOUTS

16 MIN

BINDING YES NO

### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per group

### DESCRIPTION

Divide players into groups of four with one ball per group. Two offensive players will position themselves either in the corner and wing beyond the 3PT line (on either side), or both slots beyond the 3PT line. One defender starts with a ball, a short closeout position away from the two offensive players. One more defender waits inside the smile. When the ball is passed in, the offense looks to find an open shot by shooting, driving, or passing and cutting. The defenders can attempt to steal the pass or block the shot. Offensive players only have a maximum of three dribbles. After three shots, the offense and defense switch roles. Two groups can go simultaneously at the same time on each basket.

### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- For younger players, start the offense at the short corner and elbow (closer in).
- The defender can only move after the offense completes their first pass.
- The waiting defender must start behind or beside the offensive players.

### STAFF ROLE

- Help the players with their spacings and roles (staying on offense or defense for 3 repetitions).
- Encourage defender(s) to find ways to disrupt the offense.

### SCORING

Offensive players will get 2 points or 3 points for made baskets. Defensive players will get 2 points for defensive stops (defensive rebound or forced turnover).

### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- "Was your shot a ROB shot? If not, what was missing?"
- "In what ways can the defenders disrupt the offense?"

### KEY CONCEPTS

- Creating ROB shots (Range, Open, Balanced)
- Attempting to score while maintaining the initial 2-on-1 advantage

3-ON-3 CHANGING LOCATIONS

16 MIN

BINDING YES NO

### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per basket

### DESCRIPTION

Players find a partner. Each basket needs one ball and several groups. One group will begin on offense anywhere outside the 3PT line with a second group of defenders matching up. Other groups will wait their turn at the baseline. The on-ball defender will start 'blind' to the offense, with their heels on the 3PT line facing the basket. The offense will hold the ball and place it on the defender's back. The off-ball defender can start in a gap or help position depending on their match up's placement on the 3PT line. As soon as they lift the ball from the defense's back, it becomes a live 2-on-2. Games go until a basket is scored, there is a defensive stop, or the ball goes out of bounds.

### SCORING

Offensive players will get 2 points or 3 points for made baskets. Defensive players will get 2 points for defensive stops (defensive rebound or forced turnover).

### KEY CONCEPTS

- Creating and maintaining advantage
- Attacking the help defense
- Scoring off 2-on-1 advantages
- Stunting and recovering
- Stopping the ball

Load for younger players

### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- For younger players, the lava is the paint area. Offensive players cannot catch the ball inside the paint unless they are cutting to the basket. A turnover occurs if players receive the ball in the lava (within the paint).
- Inside the 3PT line is lava. Offensive players cannot catch the ball inside the 3PT line unless they are cutting to the basket. A turnover occurs if players receive the ball in the lava (within the 3PT line).
- The offense can only score a rim finish or 3PT shot.
- For younger players, the mid-range is still permitted.
- Escape the lava. After a pass or cut is completed, the offensive player without the ball has three seconds to escape the lava (space out outside the 3PT line). If they are still inside after three seconds, a turnover is called.
- After a made basket, the next team waiting at the baseline must inbound it against the team that just scored. The defenders must pressure the ball. The offense has five seconds to complete a successful inbounds pass. Play stops if the offense is able to inbound the ball. If the defense intercepts the ball, they can score it immediately to gain additional points.

### STAFF ROLE

- Help players start from different angles and locations.
- Officiate the 'lava' load.

### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- "What other positions could you explore playing from?"
- "What can the defense do to ensure the offense does not score off the first drive?"

GAME TIME

2-ON-3-1 CONTINUOUS

16 MIN

BINDING YES NO

### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per group

### DESCRIPTION

Two offensive players will play against three defenders. The +1 will be used to help the offense but they are not allowed to score. However, this player can pass, move, set screens, etc. The offensive players will start in any location, with the defense inside the paint. As soon as the passer passes to an offensive player, the defense can closeout. The offense has 12 seconds to find a rim finish or 3PT shot.

### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- One defender is a statue and cannot move.
- One defender can only play inside the paint or outside the 3PT line.
- Use a smaller space.
- Award double points if the offense scores off an off-ball screen.

### SCORING

Offensive players will get 2 points or 3 points for made baskets.

### STAFF ROLE

- Encourage the +1 to set different types of off-ball screen (e.g. flare, screen-away, etc).

### KEY CONCEPTS

- Creating space and keeping advantage
- Disruptive defense (defensive advantage provides chance to trap)

### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- "How could you use the +1 to get open?"
- "Defense - how could you use your advantage to challenge the offense?"

Load for younger players

### 4-ON-3 CONVERT THE ADVANTAGE

16 MIN
BINDING YES NO

#### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

#### EQUIPMENT

2 balls per basket

#### DESCRIPTION

Assign players to each basket. With low numbers, have two teams of four players at each basket. With high numbers, have three teams of four players of four teams of four players at each basket. The offense must score a 3PT shot or a lay-up in 12 seconds without rotating off (we will call these 'bursts'). The offense will complete six 'bursts' against the defense with a new defense rotating in each time with groups of high numbers. Each defensive team will hold a ball, passing it into the offense to begin each 'burst'. After six 'bursts', a new team will become offense.

#### SCORING

Offensive players will get 2 points or 3 points for made baskets. Defensive players will get 2 points for defensive stops (defensive rebound or forced turnover).

#### KEY CONCEPTS

- "Make quick decisions to make the advantage greater."
- "Find a way to get to the rim for the most efficient shot."

#### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- For younger players, the lava is the paint area. Offensive players cannot catch the ball inside the paint unless they are cutting to the basket. A turnover occurs if players receive the ball in the lava (within the paint).
- Inside the 3PT line is lava. Offensive players cannot catch the ball inside the 3PT line unless they are cutting to the basket. A turnover occurs if players receive the ball in the lava (within the 3PT line).
- The offense can only score a rim finish or 3PT shot.
- For younger players, the mid-range is still permitted.
- Escape the lava. After a pass or cut is completed, the offensive player without the ball has three seconds to escape the lava (space out outside the 3PT line). If they are still inside after three seconds, a turnover is called.
- Pass and cut is a turnover. Simply convert the 4-on-3 advantage which exists.

#### STAFF ROLE

- Ensure players understand the 'bursts' concept.
- Ensure that the defenders secure the made or missed shot before rotating off to wait for their next turn.
- Ensure that the next group is primed and ready to rotate in.

#### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- "Can you find the ROB shot?"
- "In what ways can the defenders disrupt the offense?"

3-ON-3 THREE TRIPS

20 MIN

BINDING YES NO

#### PLAYING SPACE

All available full-court spaces

#### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per full-court

#### DESCRIPTION

Players will be divided up into teams of three. Ideally, there will be a maximum of five teams per basket. If there are high numbers, use the same activity but 4-on-4 or even 5-on-5. Players will begin lining up to shoot one free-throw. As soon as the free-throw is shot, a live 3-on-3 is played. If the offense secures an offensive rebound, they may immediately look to score again. If the defense secures the ball, they look to transition to the other end to begin the first 'trip.' Three trips are played, with the activity stopping after the third trip is completed.

#### SCORING

Offensive players will get 2 points or 3 points for made baskets.

#### KEY CONCEPTS

- Spacing and advantage
- Transition offense and defense

#### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- For younger players, the lava is the paint area. Offensive players cannot catch the ball inside the paint unless they are cutting to the basket. A turnover occurs if players receive the ball in the lava (within the paint).
- Inside the 3PT line is lava. Offensive players cannot catch the ball inside the 3PT line unless they are cutting to the basket. A turnover occurs if players receive the ball in the lava (within the 3PT line).
- The offense can only score a rim finish or 3PT shot.
- For younger players, the mid-range is still permitted.
- Outlet passes off a rebound are a turnover. Instead, whoever rebounds the ball must look to push the ball to start transition with greater pace.
- Scores within six seconds of gaining possession are worth double.

#### STAFF ROLE

- Help players with the free-throw line-up if needed.
- Encourage players to maintain effective spacing during the trips.

#### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- "How could we transition faster?"
- "Defensively, how should we transition back to reduce fast break opportunities?"
